mainTopic: The severity of a false שבועה, the oath ceremony, and the dispute between רב and שמואל over the two-silver-coin minimum.
overview: The גמרא first explains why a false שבועה is so serious. For ordinary sins, others are punished only if they could have protested, but for a false שבועה every group is punished more harshly, and even צדיקים get a light punishment. It then explains lines from the ברייתא about the oath ceremony. The onlookers call both sides 'wicked', because the oath rests on both of them. The court also warns the swearer that the oath follows the court's understanding, to block tricks like the reed in רבא's court. Next, רב and שמואל argue about the משנה's 'two silver coins'. רב says the denied part must be worth two מעה, while שמואל says only the whole claim must be. רבא shows that the משנה's wording leans toward רב and the פסוקים lean toward שמואל, and each side defends its reading of the words כסף and כלים. Finally, the גמרא tests both views against the cases in the משנה, and both views survive.

steps.title: Others are punished only when they could have protested
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the earlier source about people being punished for each other's sins means only people who could have protested and did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about people who had the power to protest and did not protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question raised just before. If people are punished for each other's sins in every case, what is special about a false שבועה? Its answer: for ordinary sins, others are punished only if they could have stopped it and did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets a limit on ordinary sins. Responsibility for others depends on being able to protest. A false שבועה is different, because there even people who could not protest are affected. That is what makes it more severe.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in that other source
It is in their power, they are able
To protest, to object and try to stop

phrases.english: There, it is where they had the ability to protest,
and they did not protest.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָדָם לְמַחוֹת, וְלֹא מִיחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised just before this section, which asked why a false שבועה is special if everyone is punished for each other's sins anyway.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: shared punishment for ordinary sins applies only when protest was possible.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone is punished for every sin, so a false שבועה would be no different.
steps.terutzMaskana: For ordinary sins, only those who could protest and did not are punished. A false שבועה reaches even beyond them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole contrast in the rest of the passage between ordinary sins and a false שבועה.

steps.title: How does punishment differ between family and the wider world?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference there is between the sinner's family and the rest of the world, for both רשעים and צדיקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between the wicked of his family and the wicked of the world? And between the righteous of his family and the righteous of the world?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. It wants to know exactly how punishment is divided up. It is setting up a detailed answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four groups: family רשעים, world רשעים, family צדיקים, and world צדיקים. The question is whether being family changes anything, and whether צדיקים are affected at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the world, meaning everyone else

phrases.english: What difference is there between the wicked of his family
and the wicked of the world;
between the righteous of his family
and the righteous of the world?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רְשָׁעִים דְּמִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ לָרְשָׁעִים דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 1's idea of shared punishment by asking how it is divided among groups.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The level of punishment for each group: family and world, wicked and righteous.

steps.title: How punishment is divided for ordinary sins
steps.stepSummary: For ordinary עבירות, the sinner gets his own punishment, family רשעים get a severe one, world רשעים get a light one, and all צדיקים are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: For other sins: he gets his own punishment, the wicked of the family get a severe punishment, the wicked of the world get a light punishment, and the righteous of both groups are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question for regular sins, those other than a false שבועה. It goes through each group one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Family רשעים are punished more harshly than other רשעים, because they are closer and could cover for him. צדיקים are not punished at all for ordinary sins. This is the baseline that the false שבועה will be compared to.

keyTerms.meaning: Other sins, meaning anything besides a false oath

phrases.english: He, in other sins, gets his own punishment;
and the wicked of the family get a severe punishment;
and the wicked of the world get a light punishment;
the righteous of here and here are exempt.
phrases.notes: "Here and here" means both groups: in the family and in the rest of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first half of the answer to step 2, for ordinary sins.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Ordinary sins: sinner gets his own punishment; family רשעים, severe; world רשעים, light; all צדיקים exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two lists. Here, for ordinary sins, צדיקים are completely exempt. Only in the next step, for a false שבועה, do they get a light punishment.

steps.title: How punishment is divided for a false oath
steps.stepSummary: For a false שבועה, family רשעים get the same punishment as the sinner, world רשעים get a severe one, and even צדיקים everywhere get a light one.
steps.simpleTranslation: With an oath: he and the wicked of the family get his punishment; the wicked of the world get a severe punishment; and the righteous of both groups get a light punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by giving the list for a false שבועה. Every group other than the sinner himself moves up one level compared to ordinary sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Family רשעים now share the sinner's full punishment. World רשעים go from light to severe. צדיקים go from exempt to a light punishment. This shows how much more serious a false שבועה is than other sins.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath, here a false one
Like his punishment, the same as the sinner's

steps.whatToRemember: Ordinary sin: sinner = his punishment, family רשעים = severe, world רשעים = light, צדיקים = exempt. False שבועה: sinner and family רשעים = his punishment, world רשעים = severe, צדיקים = light. Everyone except the sinner moves up one level.

phrases.aramaic: גַּבֵּי שְׁבוּעָה, הוּא וּרְשָׁעִים דְּמִשְׁפָּחָה – כְּדִינֵיהּ;
phrases.english: With regard to an oath, he and the wicked of the family get his punishment;
and the wicked of the world get a severe punishment;
and the righteous of here and here get a light punishment.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבֵּי שְׁבוּעָה, הוּא וּרְשָׁעִים דְּמִשְׁפָּחָה – כְּדִינֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by contrasting a false oath with the ordinary-sin list in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: False שבועה: sinner and family רשעים get his punishment; world רשעים, severe; all צדיקים, light.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A false שבועה is more severe than other sins. It raises the punishment of every group by one level, so even צדיקים are affected.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why a false שבועה is treated so seriously: its damage reaches the whole world, including innocent people.

steps.title: Refusing or agreeing to swear, and the onlookers' warning
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says: if the defendant refuses to swear, he is dismissed right away and must pay. If he agrees to swear, the people standing there call out 'Depart from the tents of these wicked men.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'I won't swear,' they dismiss him right away. If he says 'I will swear,' the people standing there say to each other: 'Get away from the tents of these wicked men.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא about the oath ceremony. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Refusing to swear means the defendant pays and the case ends. Agreeing to a possibly false oath is so serious that bystanders quote the פסוק said about קרח's group. Notice the plural 'men', which the גמרא will question.

keyTerms.meaning: They dismiss him (from court, and he must pay)

phrases.english: If he says: I will not take an oath,
they dismiss him immediately,
phrases.notes: He leaves court without swearing, but he has to pay the claim.

phrases.english: and if he says: I will take an oath,
the people standing there say to each other:
"Depart, I pray you, from the tents of
these wicked men."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא on the oath ceremony, after the side discussion about punishment for a false שבועה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A refuser is dismissed and pays. If he agrees to swear, the onlookers call both sides 'wicked men.'

steps.title: Why is the claimant called wicked?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why the one swearing is in danger of sinning. But why is the claimant, who only asked for the oath, included among the 'wicked men'?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who swears, since he may be doing something forbidden. But the one who makes him swear, why is he called wicked?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the plural 'wicked men' from the ברייתא. Only one person seems to be doing anything wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The swearer may be lying, so he stands near an איסור. The claimant is just using his legal right to demand an oath. So why should he be grouped with the wicked?

keyTerms.meaning: The one who makes someone else swear

phrases.english: Granted, the one who is taking the oath
stands to transgress a prohibition;
but the one who is administering the oath to him,
phrases.notes: This is the claimant, who demanded the oath.

phrases.english: why?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא הָהוּא דְּקָא מִשְׁתְּבַע קָאֵי בְּאִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the plural 'wicked men' in the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's calling both sides 'wicked men'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The claimant has done nothing wrong, so including him among the wicked seems unjustified.

steps.title: The oath rests on both of them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from רבי שמעון בן טרפון. The פסוק says 'the oath of ה׳ shall be between them both', which teaches that the oath, and its punishment, rests on both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is needed because of what a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן טרפון says, 'The oath of ה׳ shall be between them both' teaches that the oath applies to both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the claimant is also involved in the oath, so he is also included in the warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the oath is 'between them both.' From this we learn that the person who caused the oath shares responsibility for it. That is why the onlookers' warning speaks about both of them in the plural.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath in the name of ה׳

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a claimant should be careful before forcing someone to swear, because he shares in the oath.

phrases.english: That is needed for that which is taught in a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: 'That' means calling both of them wicked, in the plural.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Tarfon says:
"The oath of the Lord shall be between them both"
teaches that the oath applies to both of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source-based: a פסוק shows that both sides share the oath
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the swearer is involved in the oath, so only he could be called wicked.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oath rests on both sides, so the claimant is included in 'wicked men.'

steps.title: The court's warning: not by your understanding
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that when the court gives the oath, it tells the swearer that the oath follows the court's understanding, not his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when they make him swear, they tell him: Know that we do not make you swear according to your own understanding, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא. This sets up the question about why this warning is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The swearer cannot rely on a private meaning or a hidden trick in his words. The oath is judged by how ה׳ and the court understand it.

phrases.english: And when they administer the oath to him,
they say to him: Be aware
that it is not according to your understanding, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line goes on: but by the understanding of ה׳ and of the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court warns the swearer that his oath follows the court's understanding, not his own.

steps.title: Why does the court need to say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the court has to add this warning at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need to say this to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the court's warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath normally means what it says, so the warning seems unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know what problem it prevents.

phrases.english: Why do I need to say this to him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the court's warning

steps.title: Because of the trick with רבא's reed
steps.stepSummary: The warning exists because of the case of קניא דרבא. A defendant hid the money in a hollow reed, gave it to the claimant to hold, and swore he had 'given' him the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the reed of רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the warning prevents tricks like the one done in רבא's court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that case the swearer's words were technically true, because the money really was in the claimant's hands. But it was a deception. Since the oath follows the court's understanding, this kind of trick does not work.
steps.whatToRemember: An oath in court follows the court's understanding, so a technically true but tricky oath is still false.

phrases.english: Because of the reed of Rava.
phrases.notes: A man hid the money he owed inside a hollow stick, handed it to the claimant to hold, then swore he had given it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The warning prevents tricky oaths that are technically true, like the one in קניא דרבא.

steps.title: The משנה: the claim is two silver coins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a claim needs a value of two silver coins (מעה) for an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: The claim is two silver coins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its minimum amount. This sets up a dispute about what exactly must equal two silver coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say which part of the claim must be worth two silver coins. It could be the whole claim or the denied part. The next steps argue about this.

phrases.english: The claim is two silver coins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא and returns to the משנה's wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An oath requires a claim worth two silver coins.

steps.title: רב: the denied part must be two silver coins
steps.stepSummary: רב reads the משנה as meaning that the part the defendant denies must be worth two silver coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: the denial of the claim must be two silver coins.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains which part of the claim must be worth two silver coins: the part that is denied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the oath depends on the amount the defendant says he does not owe. If he denies less than two silver coins, there is no oath.

keyTerms.meaning: The denied part of the claim

phrases.english: Rav says:
The denial of the claim must be two silver coins.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כְּפִירַת טַעֲנָה שְׁתֵּי כֶּסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first reading of the משנה's phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The amount denied must be at least two silver coins.

steps.title: שמואל: the claim itself must be two silver coins
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says only the whole claim must be worth two silver coins. Even if the defendant denies just a פרוטה, or admits just a פרוטה, he must swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל says: the claim itself must be two silver coins. Even if he denied only a פרוטה, or admitted only a פרוטה, he must swear.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב and says the two silver coins refers to the whole claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the size of the denied part does not matter, as long as the full claim reaches two silver coins. So a claim of two מעה where only a פרוטה is denied or admitted still requires an oath.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: the denied part must be two silver coins. שמואל: only the whole claim must be two silver coins, even if a פרוטה is denied or admitted.
steps.confusionAlert: Both רב and שמואל agree on 'two silver coins'. They only argue about which part of the claim must reach that amount.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
The claim itself must be two silver coins;
even if he denied only one peruta,
or admitted only one peruta, he is liable to swear.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר טַעֲנָה עַצְמָהּ שְׁתֵּי כֶּסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's reading in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole claim must be two silver coins. A denial or admission of a פרוטה is enough for an oath.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה leans toward רב, the verses toward שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה's wording fits רב, but the פסוקים fit שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the wording of the משנה fits רב, and the verses fit שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a headline statement about the רב–שמואל argument. He is setting up the next two steps, where he will show each side's support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not decide the argument here. He points out that each side has real support: the language of the משנה backs רב, and the language of the תורה backs שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Is precise; the exact wording supports
Like him; in line with his view

phrases.english: Rava said:
The Mishnah's wording is precise in line with Rav,
and the verses are precise in line with Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא: דייקא מתניתין כוותיה דרב, וקראי כוותיה דשמואל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Evaluates the dispute between רב and שמואל from steps 12–13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's wording supports רב; the פסוקים support שמואל.

steps.title: How the משנה's wording supports רב
steps.stepSummary: Two משניות give a פרוטה minimum for the admission but never mention a פרוטה minimum for the denial, which suggests the denial must be worth more (two מעה).
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה fits רב, because it teaches that the claim must be two silver coins and the admission worth a פרוטה. It does not teach that denying a פרוטה is enough. Another משנה also teaches that the admission can be a פרוטה, but it does not say that a denial of a פרוטה is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves his first point. He shows that the משנה sets a small minimum (a פרוטה) only for the admitted part, not for the denied part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a denial of just a פרוטה were enough, the משנה should have said so, the same way it did for the admission. Its silence suggests the denied part needs the bigger amount, two מעה, which is רב's view. A second משנה shows the same pattern, so the point is stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: Admission (the part the defendant agrees he owes)
Denial (the part the defendant says he does not owe)
The smallest coin that counts as money

phrases.english: The Mishnah's wording is precise in line with Rav,
since it teaches: the claim must be two silver [coins],
and the admission worth a perutah,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ כְּפִירַת טַעֲנָה פְּרוּטָה לָא קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: whereas a denial of the claim of a perutah, it does not teach.
And we also learned [in another Mishnah]: the admission is with a perutah,
whereas a denial of a perutah, it does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: דייקא מתניתין כוותיה דרב – דקתני הטענה שתי כסף וההודאה שוה פרוטה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of רבא's headline.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that the denied part must be worth two מעה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of our משנה and a parallel משנה: both set a פרוטה minimum only for the admission.

steps.title: How the verses support שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'כסף או כלים' teaches that the claim is two מעה, and 'כי הוא זה' requires a partial admission. So the denied part can be less than two מעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verses fit שמואל, as it says: 'If a man gives his fellow silver or vessels to guard.' Just as 'vessels' means at least two, 'silver' also means at least two. Just as silver is something valuable, so is anything valuable. And the תורה says: 'that this is it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves his second point from the פסוקים. The verse fixes the minimum for the whole claim and then requires that part of it be admitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כלים' is plural, so it means at least two. Read alongside it, 'כסף' also means at least two silver coins, and this two-coin minimum applies to the whole claim. 'כי הוא זה' means the defendant admits part of it. If the entire claim is only two coins and part is admitted, the denied part must be less than two. That is שמואל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Vessels; the word is plural, so it means at least two
'That this is it': the defendant admits part of the claim

phrases.english: And the verses are precise in line with Shmuel,
as it is written: 'If a man gives his fellow
silver or vessels to guard.'
Just as 'vessels' means two,
so too 'silver' means two [coins];
just as silver is something valuable,
so too anything valuable [is included];
and the Torah says: 'that this is it.'
phrases.notes: שמות 22:8. The defendant points to part and says 'this much I owe', so he admits part and denies the rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: וקראי כוותיה דשמואל – דכתיב: כי יתן איש אל רעהו כסף או כלים לשמור
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of רבא's headline.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that only the whole claim needs to be two מעה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 22:6 ('כסף או כלים' gives a two-coin claim) together with 22:8 ('כי הוא זה' requires a partial admission).

steps.title: רב: 'This is it' only teaches partial admission
steps.stepSummary: רב says 'כי הוא זה' is needed just to teach that part must be admitted. It says nothing about how small the denial can be.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב? He needs that phrase to teach the rule of admitting part of the claim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רב answers the proof from the פסוקים. In his view, that phrase is busy teaching a different rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, 'כי הוא זה' only tells us that a שבועה requires a partial admission. He applies the two-coin minimum to the denied part, not to the whole claim. So the proof for שמואל falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)

phrases.english: And Rav? That [phrase] he needs
phrases.notes: 'That' means 'כי הוא זה' from the step before.

phrases.english: for [teaching] admission of part of the claim.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורב – ההוא מיבעי ליה להודאה במקצת הטענה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב against the proof from the פסוקים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of 'כי הוא זה' as proof that the denial can be small.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase is used up teaching that a partial admission is required, so it cannot also teach the size of the denial.

steps.title: שמואל learns two rules from 'it' and 'this'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל points out that the פסוק says both 'הוא' and 'זה'. The extra word teaches that one who denies part and admits part of a two-coin claim must swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל? It says 'it' and it says 'this.' So if he denied part and admitted part, he is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how שמואל can get both rules from the פסוק, and answers that the double wording gives him enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הוא' and 'זה' both mean roughly 'this'. That gives שמואל two words to work with: one teaches the partial admission, and the other teaches that a split within a two-coin claim is enough for a שבועה, even when the denied part is small.

phrases.english: And Shmuel?
It is written 'it' and it is written 'this,'
[teaching] that if he denied part
and admitted part, he is obligated [to swear].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב's point by finding an extra word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'כי הוא זה' is only enough to teach partial admission.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two words ('הוא' and 'זה'), enough for both rules.

steps.title: רב uses both words for other rules
steps.stepSummary: רב says one word teaches partial admission, and the other teaches that the admission must be the same kind of item as the claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב? One word is for admitting part of the claim, and one is for admitting the same kind of item as the claim.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers שמואל's extra-word argument. He shows that both words are already needed for other rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the second word teaches 'ממין הטענה'. For example, if the claim is for wheat, the admission must also be wheat, not barley. Since both words are already in use, there is nothing left over to teach שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the same kind of item as the claim

phrases.english: And Rav? One is for admission of part of the claim,
and one is for admission of the same kind as the claim.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורב – חד להודאה במקצת הטענה, וחד להודאה ממין הטענה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on שמואל's reading of the double wording.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of the second word for שמואל's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The second word is needed for the rule of 'ממין הטענה'.

steps.title: שמואל: my rule follows automatically
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says he does not need an extra word. If the claim is two מעה and part is admitted, the denied part is less than two on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל? Don't you learn it automatically, since the admission makes the claim smaller?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers that his rule needs no special source. It comes out on its own from the basic rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim only needs to be two coins, and the תורה requires part of it to be admitted. That admission takes something away from the claim, so what is left to be denied must be less than two coins. שמואל's view is built into the פסוק itself.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the משנה's wording leans toward רב (it never gives a small minimum for the denial), but the פסוקים lean toward שמואל. A two-coin claim with a partial admission automatically leaves a denial of less than two coins.

phrases.english: And Shmuel? Don't you hear it from this automatically,
that [the admission] makes the claim smaller?

steps.triggerLanguage: ושמואל – לאו ממילא שמעת מיניה דחסרה לה טענה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל answers רב by showing he never needed the extra word.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical consequence, so no extra source is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל needs a spare word in the פסוק for his rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: His rule follows automatically from a two-coin claim combined with a required partial admission.

steps.title: רב explains that the word כסף teaches about the denial
steps.stepSummary: רב answers שמואל: the word כלים already teaches that the claim must be two, so the extra word כסף must be teaching that the denial must be two silver מעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב could say: the word 'silver' came from the start to teach about the denial. If it were about the claim, the תורה could have just written 'If a man gives his fellow vessels to guard,' and we would learn that just as 'vessels' means at least two, any claim must be at least two. So why did the תורה write 'silver'? If it is not needed for the claim, use it for the denial.
steps.whatsHappening: רב defends his view by showing that the word כסף in the פסוק is not needed for the claim, so it must be teaching a rule about the denial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל had said that כסף teaches the claim is two מעה. רב replies that the word כלים already teaches 'two' for the claim. Since כסף adds nothing to the claim, רב moves it over to the denial: the denied part must be worth two silver מעה.

keyTerms.meaning: Denial: the part of the claim the defendant says he does not owe
Claim: what the claimant says is owed to him
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Vessels; the plural form tells us there are at least two

keyTerms.term: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְ... תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְ...
keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for this topic, apply it to that topic

phrases.english: Rather, רב could say to you:
When the word 'silver' came originally,
it came to teach about the denial;
for if it were about the claim, let the Torah write:
'If a man gives to his fellow
phrases.notes: שמות 22:6, but without the word כסף.

phrases.english: vessels to guard,'
and I would say: just as 'vessels' means two,
so too any claim must be for two;
so why do I need 'silver' that the Torah wrote?
If it is not needed for the claim,
apply it to the denial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב responds to שמואל's claim in step 20 by giving his own reading of the word כסף.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: the word כסף is redirected from the claim to the denial
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל thought כסף teaches the claim must be two מעה, leaving the denial with no minimum.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since כלים already teaches 'two' for the claim, כסף is free to teach that the denial must be two silver מעה.

steps.title: שמואל says כסף teaches the claim must be for something valuable
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that כסף is still needed for the claim: without it, we might think any two items count, even worthless ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל could say to you: if the תורה had written only 'vessels' and not 'silver', I would have said that just as vessels are two, any claim must be for two, but it does not need to be something valuable. So 'silver' teaches us that it must be.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל pushes back on רב by showing that the word כסף does have a job in the claim, so it cannot be moved over to the denial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's argument depended on כסף being extra for the claim. שמואל says it is not extra: כלים teaches the number two, and כסף teaches that the items must have real value, like silver. So רב's derivation for the denial falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)

phrases.english: And שמואל could say to you:
If the Torah had written 'vessels'
and not written 'silver', I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי כֵּלִים שְׁנַיִם, אַף כֹּל שְׁנַיִם –
phrases.english: just as vessels are two, so too any claim is two,
but we do not need something of real value;
so the word 'silver' teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל rejects רב's claim in step 21 that כסף is extra for the claim.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב's derivation that the denial must be two מעה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב assumed כסף adds nothing to the claim, but it teaches that the claim must be for something of real value.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that כלים teaches 'two'. They argue over whether כסף teaches that the claim must have real value (שמואל) or that the denial must be two מעה (רב).

steps.title: A challenge to שמואל from the משנה about admitting a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if someone is claimed two silver coins and admits only a פרוטה, he is exempt. That seems to be because the denied part is less than two מעה, which goes against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'I have two silver coins in your hand.' 'You have only a פרוטה in my hand.' He is exempt. What is the reason? Is it not because the denied part is less than the required amount? Then this is a refutation of שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a case from our משנה that seems to support רב and disprove שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the defendant admits a פרוטה, so he denies two מעה minus a פרוטה, which is less than two מעה. The משנה says he does not swear. That fits רב, who needs two מעה denied, but seems to contradict שמואל, who does not require the denial to be two מעה.

keyTerms.meaning: A small copper coin, the smallest amount of money
A strong refutation that seems to disprove someone's view

phrases.english: We learned: 'I have two silver coins in your hand,'
'You have only a פרוטה in my hand': he is exempt.
What is the reason?
Is it not because the claim is lacking?
And that is a refutation of שמואל?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the argument from the פסוק, the גמרא turns to the משנה to test שמואל's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that the denial does not need to be two מעה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה exempts someone whose denial is less than two מעה, which shows a minimum is needed for the denial.

steps.title: שמואל says the משנה means actual silver coins
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the משנה is about actual silver coins. The defendant admitted a copper פרוטה, which is a different item, so this is not a partial admission at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל could say to you: Do you think the משנה means the value of two silver coins? It means exactly silver coins. What he claimed, the other did not admit, and what he admitted, the claimant did not claim.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge by reading the משנה as a case where the admission was a different kind of item than the claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the claim was for two מעה worth of anything, so admitting a פרוטה was a real partial admission. שמואל says the claim was for actual silver coins, while the admission was a copper פרוטה. What he admitted was never claimed, so there is no partial admission at all. That is why he is exempt, not because the denial is too small.

keyTerms.meaning: What he claimed, the other did not admit

phrases.english: שמואל could say to you:
Do you think it teaches the value?!
phrases.notes: He means: do you think the claim was for anything worth two silver coins?

phrases.english: It teaches exactly that,
phrases.notes: Actual silver coins were claimed, while the admission was a copper פרוטה.

phrases.english: what he claimed from him, he did not admit to him,
and what he admitted to him, he had not claimed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ שְׁמוּאֵל: מִי סָבְרַתְּ שָׁוֶה קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to שמואל in step 23 by redefining the case in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the claim was for actual silver coins, not their value
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The defendant is exempt because his denial was less than two מעה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The defendant is exempt because he admitted a different item (copper) than what was claimed (silver), so there is no partial admission at all.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying the denial was too small. He is saying the admission does not count, because it was a different kind of item from what was claimed.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about the פרוטה does not disprove שמואל: the claim was for actual silver, and admitting copper is not a partial admission of that claim.

steps.title: The next case in the משנה seems to break the 'actual coins' reading
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה means actual silver coins, why is a person liable when claimed two silver and a פרוטה and he admits only the פרוטה? What he admitted (copper) seems different from what was claimed (silver).
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the next case: 'You have two silver and a פרוטה of mine.' 'You only have a פרוטה.' He is liable. If the claim is about value, that makes sense. But if it is about actual coins, why is he liable? What he claimed was not admitted, and what was admitted was not claimed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's answer from step 24 by quoting the next case in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24, שמואל said a copper פרוטה is a different item from silver coins, so admitting it is no admission at all. But in the next case the defendant admits a פרוטה and is liable. If the coins are 'specific', the same logic should exempt him here too. Only the 'value' reading (שוה) seems to explain the liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Look at the later part of the משנה
Value: the claim is for coins worth two silver מעה, not the actual coins
Specifically: the claim is for the actual silver coins

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. In the first case only two silver were claimed and he was exempt. Here a פרוטה was also claimed, and he is liable.

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:
"I have two silver and a פרוטה in your hand,"
"You have only a פרוטה in my hand" — he is liable.
It works out if you say it means value —
that is why he is liable;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ דַּוְקָא – אַמַּאי חַיָּיב?
phrases.english: but if you say it means specifically, why is he liable?
What he claimed from him, he did not admit to him,
and what he admitted to him, he did not claim from him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's 'actual coins' answer from step 24 using the next case in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reading that the משנה is about actual silver coins (דוקא)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If silver and copper are different items, admitting the copper פרוטה should not count, yet the משנה makes him liable.

steps.title: By שמואל's own rule, admitting one of two claimed items makes you liable
steps.stepSummary: This discussion is only about שמואל, and שמואל holds that if someone is claimed wheat and barley and admits one of them, he is liable. Here too, silver and a פרוטה were claimed and the פרוטה was admitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this only a question on שמואל? But רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: if he claimed wheat and barley from him and he admitted one of them, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by bringing another ruling of שמואל that fits the second case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case only silver was claimed, so admitting copper was admitting something never claimed. In the second case the פרוטה was part of the claim, so admitting it is like admitting the barley out of 'wheat and barley'. Since he denied the two silver, he is liable even on the 'actual coins' reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't this whole question only about שמואל's view?
Wheat and barley: two different items claimed together

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the key difference: admitting an item that was never claimed does not count, but admitting one of several claimed items does.

phrases.english: Isn't the issue only according to שמואל?
But didn't רב נחמן say that שמואל said:
If he claimed wheat and barley from him
and he admitted to him one of them — he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a separate ruling of the same אמורא that explains the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Admitting a copper פרוטה can never count when silver was claimed, so liability in the second case must mean the משנה is about value.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the פרוטה itself was part of the claim, admitting it is admitting one of the claimed items, like wheat and barley, so he is liable even if the coins are specific.

steps.title: Proof from the gold-and-silver case that the משנה means actual coins
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says if he claimed a ליטרא of gold and the defendant admitted a ליטרא of silver, he is exempt. That only makes sense if the claim is for the actual metal, since a ליטרא is worth far more than two מעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense, since the later part teaches: 'I have a ליטרא of gold in your hand.' 'You only have a ליטרא of silver.' He is exempt. If it means specifically, that is why he is exempt. But if it means value, why is he exempt? A ליטרא is a lot!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings support for the 'actual coins' (דוקא) reading from another case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If claims were only about value, a gold ליטרא claim with a silver ליטרא admission would be a partial admission of a large amount, and he should be liable. The משנה exempts him, so it must treat gold and silver as different items. That means the משנה reads claims as 'specific'.

keyTerms.meaning: This also stands to reason: introduces support
A ליטרא, a large weight of metal

phrases.english: This also stands to reason —
from the fact that the latter clause teaches:
"I have a ליטרא of gold in your hand,"

phrases.aramaic: ״אֵין לְךָ בְּיָדִי אֶלָּא לִיטְרָא כֶּסֶף״ – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: "You have only a ליטרא of silver in my hand" — he is exempt.
It works out if you say it teaches specifically —
that is why he is exempt;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ שָׁוֶה – אַמַּאי פָּטוּר?
phrases.english: but if you say it means value, why is he exempt?
A ליטרא is a lot!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the 'actual coins' reading, the גמרא brings positive support for it.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה reads claims as specific items (דוקא), as שמואל said
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that a gold ליטרא claim with a silver ליטרא admission is exempt

steps.title: Since the later case means actual coins, the first case does too
steps.stepSummary: Because the later case of the משנה is clearly about specific items, the first case is also about specific silver coins, just as שמואל said.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since the later part means specifically, the first part also means specifically.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the proof: the whole משנה is read as talking about specific coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gold case proves the משנה treats claims as specific. We read the first case the same way, so the exemption there is because copper was never claimed, not because the denied part was under two מעה. The challenge against שמואל from step 23 is fully answered.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
From the fact that the later part

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is about actual silver coins (דוקא). Admitting copper when only silver was claimed is not a partial admission, but admitting one of several claimed items is. So the משנה does not contradict שמואל.

phrases.english: Rather, since the latter clause means specifically,
the first clause also means specifically.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִדְּסֵיפָא דַּוְקָא, רֵישָׁא נָמֵי דַּוְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in step 27.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The whole משנה is about specific coins, so the first case's exemption fits שמואל's view.

steps.title: Is this a refutation of רב?
steps.stepSummary: Since the ליטרא of gold case showed the משנה is about actual items, the גמרא asks whether רב's view, that the משנה is about value, is now disproven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the proof it just brought for שמואל and turns it against רב, asking if רב's reading of the משנה is now knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב read the משנה as speaking about the value of silver, not actual silver coins. If the ליטרא of gold case proves the whole משנה is about actual items, then רב's reading no longer fits. The word לֵימָא signals a suggestion that may still be pushed back.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion the גמרא may later reject.
A strong refutation that knocks down a view.

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the proof that supported שמואל into a challenge against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's reading that the משנה speaks of the value of silver.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ליטרא of gold case proves the whole משנה is about actual items, רב's reading in terms of value cannot be right.

steps.title: רב says only the gold case is different
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the whole משנה is about value, and only the ליטרא of gold case is about actual metal, so it proves nothing about the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can tell you: the whole משנה is about value, but a ליטרא of gold is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by saying the gold case is an exception and does not show how to read the rest of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof for שמואל assumed that if one case is about actual items, the whole משנה must be too. רב rejects that link. A ליטרא is a measure of weight, not a coin, so that one case is naturally about actual gold. The other cases, which speak of coins, can still be about value.

keyTerms.meaning: Worth or value. Here it means the claim is for the value of silver, not the actual coins.
A unit of weight, not a coin.
It is different, so it is an exception that does not teach about other cases.

steps.whatToRemember: רב survives the challenge. In his view the משנה is about value, and only the ליטרא of gold case is about an actual item, because a ליטרא is a weight and not a coin.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב admits the משנה is about actual items. He only says the gold case is an exception. Every other case in the משנה is still about value for him.

phrases.english: רב can say to you:
the entire משנה is about value,
but a ליטרא of gold is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב by making the gold case an exception.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the gold case is an exception and does not decide how to read the rest of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ליטרא of gold case shows the whole משנה is about actual items, which disproves רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the ליטרא of gold case is about an actual item, since a ליטרא is a weight. The rest of the משנה is about value, so רב's view stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both רב and שמואל remain possible readings of the משנה. The gold case alone does not settle their disagreement.
